title: Henry of Navarre to Ségur, BnF 500 de Colbert 401 ff. 233, 239, 288v (1585-86), Navarre key A

steps.what: Gallica IIIF fetched with a browser User-Agent.
ff. 233, 239, 288v transcribed from full-resolution images (and f. 143, now segur1583).
Frequencies of the upper figures mod 5 show blocks of five: an alphabetical syllabary.
Catherine de Médicis letters under random keys of the same shape; 64-start model 47-90 %, corrected 54-start model 96.6 %.
Structured annealer with the clear French as context recovers the key; syllabary start corrected from 64 to 54 by the reading.
Three letters read in substance; word-signs partly glossed.
Whole volume swept for further letters in this key: none; f. 366 found (probably this key). (The f. 333 reading with Tomokiyo's f. 321 key in the same session is now navarre1586.)
f. 366 (24 tokens) tried with both keys; two of three lines do not read.
Design-constrained annealer (alphabetical homophone counts) on the ff. 233 set: whole letter key from seed 0, 287 of 290 letter tokens (99.0 %) against key_v4.json.

Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): he wrote that he had independently solved it in 2024 but never published it; kept in the ciphertext-only list with that note. In Oct 2026 he specified that his saved decryptions (15 Oct 2024) cover ff. 143, 233, 239 and 288v.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 470 tokens, 103 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.066 per letter; random keys -4.259 (z 15.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.698 (mean -2.734, z 17.4); annealer on the real text -2.564. Verdict: pass.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): segur keeps key A (ff. 233, 239, 288v; f. 366 noted as 'probably this key', open, and kept out of documents[] because its key is not shown); f. 333 with Tomokiyo's f. 321 key moved to navarre1586; f. 143 (1583, another key) moved to segur1583.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.066; polyphony 0.0; 16 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.564

outcome.method_basis: A syllabary residue test and a structured annealer with the letters' clear French as language-model context rebuilt the ff. 233/239/288v key, confirmed on matched controls; Tomokiyo's sibling f. 321 key (on cryptiana before the attempt) has different offsets and was not used for these letters.
outcome.notes: ff. 233, 239, 288v read in substance; word-signs and numbers 180, 215?, 900 open. f. 366 (probably this key) left open and outside the documents; f. 333 (Tomokiyo's f. 321 key) is navarre1586; f. 143 (1583, another key) is segur1583.

credits.note: saved decryptions of ff. 233, 239, 288v dated 15 Oct 2024 (with f. 143, another key; see segur1583), unpublished

outcome.fraction_read_source: validation.tsv (mk_validation.py, ff. 233/239/288v with key_v4.json): 482 non-null tokens, 466 with a value, 16 unread word-signs and numbers (X, gla, gna, pe, pu, e, H, L, Ne, qua, 180, 215?, 900); glossed word-signs counted with their gloss.

gaps.item: word-signs X, gla, gna, pe, pu, e, H, L, Ne, qua and numbers 180, 215?, 900
gaps.detail: no gloss in this volume (whole volume swept); the key sheet and 500 Colbert 402 are not available; LM ranking only suggests classes

gaps.item: f. 366 (24 tokens, probably this key), lines 1-2
gaps.detail: line 3 reads escri; lines 1-2 decode to non-French, probably names in the king's spelling

prior.where: No plaintext of ff. 233, 239, 288v found in print or online. George Lasry's saved decryptions of 15 Oct 2024 cover ff. 143, 233, 239 and 288v (his note to the project, Oct 2026); unpublished; earlier reported 25 Sept 2026 as an independent 2024 solution. Tomokiyo's f. 321 key (a sibling, different values) was on cryptiana.

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
